name: Narendra Modi
text: Start-ups have a huge opportunity for collaboration with small local businesses. Start-ups can empower and make these local businesses efficient.

name: Satya Nadella
text: Nadella described digital infrastructure, connectivity and AI as an opportunity to improve productivity, including for small businesses, while extending technological benefits across countries.

name: Sundar Pichai
text: Pichai called for broader connectivity, financial inclusion and digital skills, highlighting the importance of giving small businesses access to digital tools and opportunities to grow across borders.

name: Muhammad Yunus
role: Founder, Grameen Bank · 2006 Nobel Peace Prize laureate
text: In a lecture on social business and microcredit, Yunus discussed empowering women and reducing poverty, describing how encouragement and access to small loans can help people take their first steps in business.
event: Social Business and Microcredit for Women’s Empowerment and Poverty Alleviation · Georgetown University

name: Jack Ma
text: At the launch of the Enabling E-commerce initiative, Ma advocated a more inclusive global marketplace in which small businesses, young people and developing countries can participate and succeed.
event: Enabling E-commerce initiative launch · Buenos Aires

name: Ajay Banga
text: Banga described how digital payments, business data and digital solutions can help MSMEs become visible to lenders, connect to markets and overcome barriers to finance and growth.
event: MSMEs: Leveraging Data for Jobs · World Bank Group Annual Meetings, Bangkok
connection: Relevant to small-business empowerment: accessible digital records and tools can support everyday operations, market access and opportunities to grow.

name: Josephine Teo
role: Minister for Digital Development and Information, Singapore
text: Teo emphasized that SME success with AI depends on tools that fit real business needs, accessible data, capable people and support to integrate technology into everyday workflows. Adoption alone is not the goal; tangible business impact matters.
event: Keynote address · SMEs Go Digital Day 2026
publisher: Ministry of Digital Development and Information, Singapore
connection: Relevant to productivity: practical tools should fit small-business workflows and resources, helping owners serve customers and compete more effectively.

name: Sundar Pichai
text: Pichai urged investment in connectivity, computing infrastructure and training so that the digital divide does not deepen into an AI divide. He called on companies of every size to use AI to innovate and empower workers.
event: Opening ceremony · AI Impact Summit, New Delhi, India
sourceType: Official transcript · As prepared for delivery
connection: Relevant to digital access: infrastructure, skills and language inclusion can broaden the opportunity for smaller businesses to benefit from technology.

name: Doreen Bogdan-Martin
text: Bogdan-Martin connected inclusive economic growth with meaningful access to digital tools for learning, doing business and participating safely in the global economy. She warned that unequal connectivity and computing capacity risk widening the AI divide.
event: G20 Leaders’ Summit · Sessions One and Three, Johannesburg Expo Centre, South Africa
sourceType: Official statements · As prepared for delivery
connection: Relevant to global commerce: meaningful connectivity helps businesses participate in the digital economy, wherever they operate.
